variants.headline: Ordered goods reach the dock
variants.sub: Imported {good} ordered by {company} has landed at the colony's port.
variants.body:
The company {company} has received {qty} units of {good} at the port. The order arrived a full round trip after it was placed and was paid for on the dock. For {target}, the event is a practical test of the connection between ordering, waiting and obtaining goods.

People live through the interval between an order and its arrival. Working people's needs belong at the centre of this discussion, rather than outside its political argument.

variants.headline: An order completes its long journey
variants.sub: The company {company} has taken delivery of its home-world order of {good}.
variants.body:
A full round trip separates an order from its delivery: {company} has received {qty} units of {good} from the home world. Payment was made on the dock. Readers considering {target} should keep the long interval in view when judging what responsible provision for the colony requires.

People live through the interval between an order and its arrival. Working people's needs belong at the centre of this discussion, rather than outside its political argument.

variants.headline: Imports landed and paid for
variants.sub: The company {company} has received its imported order of {good} at the port.
variants.body:
The dock has become the point where a distant order is finally delivered and paid: {company} has received {qty} units of {good}. A full round trip has passed since the order. The question for {target} concerns practical provision across that distance, rather than an instant answer to need.

People live through the interval between an order and its arrival. Working people's needs belong at the centre of this discussion, rather than outside its political argument.
